correctness.rationale: Every multiplier is computed from the normalized unit-period Fourier basis; counting keeps both signs of each n and removes zeros. The fixed rational law follows from residue Riemann sums, the irrational law from equidistribution for a two-variable Riemann-integrable indicator, and the critical law from fixed-period residue Riemann sums under alpha(t)=a/b+lambda*t. Analytic nonzero level functions make boundaries measure zero; continuous periodic averaging gives the large-detuning limit. The explicit b=2 branch yields the strict dip, and monotone inversion yields ks_k and Schatten residue. Recomputed deterministic frequency tests pass; experiments are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Counts of singular modes above a threshold directly determine rank budgets for periodic boxcar deblurring. Rational windows have exactly lost frequencies but the global sharp count loses a denominator-dependent proportion; irrational windows have a universal normalized Weyl density. At calibration error comparable to the singular threshold, neither fixed law applies: the explicit detuning curve and strict half-window spectral dip give a structural and nonobvious answer of independent use, not merely a restatement of the standard sinc formula.
